q.intro.text: A diver swims down at a steady pace: her height changes by negative four feet every minute.

q.ask.text: Right now she is at the marker. Compared with now, where was she three minutes ago?

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the notation.

e.s1.text: Every minute is one equal jump of negative four feet: four feet down.

e.s2.text: Later is positive time. In three minutes she makes three jumps of negative four: three times negative four is negative twelve. One negative factor: a negative product.

e.s3.text: Earlier is negative time. The three jumps before now brought her down to the marker, so three minutes ago she was twelve feet higher: negative three times negative four is twelve.

e.s4.text: Division undoes it: twelve divided by negative three is negative four, because negative three times negative four is twelve. Same signs: positive. Different signs: negative.

e.why.text: Quick check: why is negative three times negative four positive?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. Going back three minutes undoes three drops of four feet, so she was twelve feet higher than now.

e.w-add.text: Careful: two negatives added stay negative, negative three plus negative four is negative seven. The picture shows why the product is positive.

e.w-rule.text: It has a reason: going back in time undoes the drops, so she was twelve feet higher.

t.intro.text: A cold front: the temperature changes by negative one point five degrees every hour. It is thirty degrees now. The first two steps are done for you.

t.count.text: Your step: compared with now, how much warmer or colder was it four hours ago? Warmer is plus, colder is minus.

t.fill.text: Type a number. Use a minus sign for colder.

t.c-ok.text: Yes: the four drops of one point five degrees came after, so four hours ago it was six degrees warmer: plus six.

t.c-neg.text: Look at the jumps: they lead down to now. Before them it was warmer, so the change is plus six, not negative six.

t.c-add.text: That adds negative four and negative one point five. Four hours of negative one point five degrees each is a product.

t.c-other.text: Count the jumps from four hours ago to now: four jumps of one point five degrees each.

t.write.text: Tap the chips to write it as one multiplication.

t.w-ok.text: Yes: negative four times negative one point five is six. Two negative factors, a positive product.

t.w-add.text: That adds. Four hours of the same change is times.

t.w-later.text: Four times negative one point five is four hours from now: negative six. Hours ago are negative time: negative four.

t.w-other.text: Use the time, where hours ago are negative, and the change per hour.

t.div.text: Now divide: six divided by negative four. Use the multiplication you just wrote.

t.d-ok.text: Right: negative four times negative one point five is six, so six divided by negative four is negative one point five, the change per hour. Different signs: a negative quotient.

t.d-no.text: Check it: negative four times one point five is negative six, not six. The quotient is negative one point five: different signs, negative.

t.cb-right.text: At the start you picked plus twelve feet, and you were right. Now you can show why.

t.cb-neg.text: At the start you picked negative twelve feet: that is where she will be three minutes from now. Three minutes ago she was twelve feet higher.

t.cb-add.text: At the start you picked negative seven feet: that adds negative three and negative four. It is a product: negative three times negative four is plus twelve.

p.intro.text: Jordan says: negative three times negative four is negative twelve, because a negative times anything stays negative.

p.test.text: Let's test it. Build the argument and see where it leads.

p.prove.text: Now prove it, without the diver. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.c1.text: Negative three times the sum four plus negative four is zero,

p.c2.text: and it also equals negative three times four, plus negative three times negative four,

p.c3.text: where negative three times four is negative twelve,

p.c4.text: so negative twelve plus negative three times negative four is zero, and negative three times negative four is twelve.

p.x-any.text: That is Jordan's idea, the one being tested. It cannot be a reason here.

p.x-add.text: That adds. Every line here is about products.

p.x-examples.text: One example is not a reason: a reason must work for every number.

p.x-rule.text: That uses the rule to prove the rule. Find what makes this line true.

p.x-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line.

p.done.text: That's a proof: four claims, each with its reason, and the scale backs every one. The distributive property forces negative times negative to be positive.
